newsitem.title: USA: Calif. names underwriters for utility bond deal.
newsitem.headline: Calif. names underwriters for utility bond deal.

text.p: California's treasurer said Wednesday he tapped Lehman Brother, Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers to underwrite the upcoming sale of up to $6 billion of bonds as part of the state's plan to deregulate its electricity market.

State Treasurer Matt Fong said Lehman would serve as co-senior manager, along with Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers, for the so-called "rate reduction bonds" that will be sold later this year. The bonds will be issued by the state's infrastructure bank, Fong's office said.
The bonds will be sold on behalf of PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co, Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, and Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co.
The bonds will help offset the so-called stranded costs facing the utilities, such as nuclear power plants that would not be economical in a competitive market.
The bonds are a critical part of California's plan to throw open its $20 billion electricity market to competition next January, state officials said.
"These bonds are an important part of a deregulation process that will result in lower utility costs for Californians," Fong said in a statement.

Fong's office said Lehman Brothers and Morgan Stanley would handle the Pacific Gas & Electric bonds; Lehman and Salomon would handle the Southern California Edison issue; and Lehman and Morgan Stanley would handle the San Diego Gas & Electric sale.
